Discuss your bookkeeping needs
Current books. Supported balances. A usable month-end.
When this service fits
You may be keeping up with invoicing but falling behind on the ledger, inheriting unreconciled balances, or spending each month rebuilding the same spreadsheets. This service suits owners and finance managers who need the accounting work completed consistently and a clear explanation of what still needs attention.
What the work covers
The starting point matters. A current ledger may need a recurring monthly service. A backlog needs an initial cleanup plan covering the affected periods, available evidence and opening balances before recurring work begins.
Record sales, purchases, receipts and payments against the supporting documents.
Reconcile bank and card balances, investigate unmatched transactions and identify duplicate entries.
Review customer and supplier balances, including overdue items, unapplied receipts and credits.
Prepare schedules for agreed accruals, prepayments, fixed assets and other close adjustments.
Maintain a month-end checklist and a list of missing documents or unresolved balances.
What you receive
An agreed close pack: the trial balance or ledger export, bank reconciliation summaries, customer and supplier ageing, supporting balance schedules and an open-items list. Each unresolved item should identify the evidence needed, its owner and whether it affects the figures being reported.
Management accounts and tax return preparation can build on these records, but are separate outputs to agree rather than assumed parts of every bookkeeping engagement.
How the work moves
Establish the baseline. Confirm the entity, period, accounting basis, opening balances and records available.
Post and reconcile. Match transactions to evidence and reconcile balances to independent records.
Resolve exceptions. Bring missing invoices, unexplained transfers and accounting judgments into one review list.
Complete the close. Record agreed adjustments and hand over the completed schedules with remaining issues clearly identified.
An example of the work
Illustrative example, not a client result: a bank statement shows a customer receipt of AED 10,000, but the ledger still shows two unpaid invoices of AED 6,000 and AED 4,000. Checking the remittance may show that one payment settles both invoices. Matching the receipt correctly clears the customer balance without recording revenue a second time. If the remittance is missing, the receipt stays on the exceptions list until its allocation is supported.
What to have ready
Your accounting system, the last completed period, bank and card statements, sales and purchase records, payroll summaries, loan schedules and any previous reconciliation files. For an initial enquiry, describe the records and the periods involved; document access is arranged separately.
Choose focused support or a connected finance scope
Bookkeeping is the transaction and reconciliation foundation. Dedicated month-end and year-end close support organizes period-end adjustments and the final handover. Accounts receivable and accounts payable services focus on customer and supplier balances, follow-up and review-ready schedules. They can be engaged individually without assuming that a whole finance function is being outsourced.
Full finance department outsourcing connects agreed recurring workstreams through a responsibility map and operating calendar. A fractional controller adds operational oversight of close quality, controls and reporting. Fractional CFO advisory addresses leadership decisions and financial direction. The engagement specifies which of these responsibilities is actually included.
Can you take over books that are several months behind?
Yes. The first step is to identify which periods are incomplete and whether the opening balances can be supported. Cleanup may be staged so the oldest unresolved balances do not get carried into each new month. The proposed scope should distinguish catch-up work from ongoing bookkeeping.
Are bank feeds enough to complete the books?
Bank feeds help identify money movements. They do not explain every transaction, establish the correct accounting treatment or replace invoices and other evidence. Transfers, customer deposits, loan receipts and equipment purchases need different treatment even though each appears in a bank feed.
Can our staff keep invoicing and paying suppliers?
Yes. The work can sit alongside those responsibilities. Agree who creates invoices, records bills, resolves supplier queries and makes payments so the same transaction is not entered twice or missed between teams.
What determines the scope and fee?
The number of entities and accounts, transaction complexity, quality of opening balances, months of cleanup and required close outputs. Transaction volume matters, but an unreconciled balance or complex inventory process can require more work than the raw number of transactions suggests.

Can every transaction be automated?
Rules work best for repeatable transactions with reliable inputs. Unusual items, missing evidence and accounting judgments still need review. The process should identify these exceptions instead of giving them an automatic treatment that is difficult to trace.
What happens after setup?
The handover defines the routine and its owner. Ongoing bookkeeping, support after a platform change and additional integrations are agreed separately so the team knows what maintenance is included.

Know the movement. Understand the driver.
When this service fits
You receive reports but cannot easily explain why margin changed, where cash is tied up or whether the business is performing against plan. Different departments may also be using different definitions of the same measure. Management information systems, or MIS, should give those conversations a common basis.
Start with the decision, then choose the report
A founder reviewing growth may need revenue, gross margin and hiring costs together. An operations manager may need project profitability and cost overruns. A leadership team may need a concise pack that links the income statement to receivables, commitments and cash.
The report design starts with those decisions and the quality of available data. It does not start with a long list of dashboard widgets.
What the work covers
Structure management accounts with meaningful comparison periods.
Define KPIs, their calculation, source, reporting frequency and owner.
Compare actual results with budgets, forecasts or prior periods.
Investigate material movements and distinguish recurring changes from one-off items.
Add commentary, open data issues and actions for the management review.
What you receive
An agreed management pack, a KPI definition sheet and commentary on the material movements. Depending on the scope, the pack may include the profit and loss, balance sheet, cash summary, receivables ageing and department or project analysis where the records support it.
For each key measure, the reader should be able to identify the period, comparison, source and any estimate. This is management reporting, not an audit or assurance opinion.
A reporting example
Illustrative example: monthly revenue rises from AED 200,000 to AED 240,000, while direct costs rise from AED 120,000 to AED 156,000. Gross profit increases from AED 80,000 to AED 84,000, but gross margin falls from 40% to 35%. A useful report shows both movements and investigates price, sales mix and delivery costs. The figures alone do not establish which driver caused the change.
How the work moves
Define the questions and measures. Check that the underlying accounts and operational data support them. Prepare a consistent pack, investigate the important variances and record the decisions or follow-up needed. Refresh the definitions when the business changes rather than silently changing a measure mid-series.
Board and investor reporting with a clear basis
A separately agreed board or investor reporting pack can connect management accounts, operating KPIs, runway and cash, forecast changes and decisions requiring attention. We agree the audience, reporting period, metric definitions and narrative before assembling the pack. Unreconciled balances, estimates and changing definitions remain visible rather than being hidden behind a polished presentation.
Profitability and unit economics analysis can examine a customer, product, project or channel when revenue, direct cost and allocation data support it. Contribution margin, acquisition cost or payback measures need a consistent definition and appropriate context; not every business can calculate them reliably from the information already in its ledger. The output is a traceable calculation and practical commentary, not an assurance opinion or a promise of investor acceptance.
What is the difference between bookkeeping and MIS?
Bookkeeping records and reconciles transactions. MIS organizes that information around management decisions, adds comparisons and explains movements. Where the books are incomplete, the reporting scope needs to address the missing foundation first.
Can you improve our existing reports?
Yes. We can start with the pack already used, identify duplicated reports and find the questions it leaves unanswered. Retaining a familiar format may be better than introducing a new dashboard the team will not maintain.
Can reports show results by customer, project or department?
They can when the underlying records contain a reliable way to allocate income and costs. We first check the coding and allocation approach. Estimates should be identified rather than presented as precise segment results.
How often should we receive a pack?
The reporting rhythm follows the decisions being made and the availability of reliable inputs. Monthly management reporting may be paired with a more frequent cash view. The reporting calendar is agreed with the people responsible for supplying and reviewing the data.

Build a driver-based budget, rolling forecast and useful scenarios. Explore financial planning with documented assumptions and actual-versus-plan reviews.
/finance/services/budgeting-forecasting
Build a financial plan you can explain and update.
Connect revenue, costs, headcount and investment plans to the assumptions behind them. LedgerByte supports budgets, rolling forecasts and scenarios that remain useful when trading conditions change.
Discuss your planning needs
Clear drivers. Visible assumptions. Better planning conversations.
When this service fits
You are preparing an annual plan, considering a new hire or location, or replacing a forecast that no longer reflects the business. The work suits teams that need to understand what must happen for a plan to work and what changes when an assumption moves.
Budget, forecast and scenario: three different jobs
A budget sets an agreed plan and a comparison point. A forecast updates the expected outcome using what is now known. A scenario tests a specific alternative, such as slower sales, a hiring delay or a supplier price increase. Keeping these separate avoids rewriting the original target every time expectations change.
What the work covers
Identify the drivers of revenue, direct costs, overheads, headcount and investment.
Build an annual budget or a defined forecast horizon.
Connect the plan to historical actuals and known commitments.
Model selected upside and downside cases with explicit assumptions.
Review actual-versus-plan differences and document forecast changes.
What you receive
A working budget or forecast model, an assumptions register, selected scenario outputs and an update schedule. Assumptions should show their source, owner and date. Where the engagement includes balance-sheet and cash-flow forecasting, those links are specified rather than implied by a profit-and-loss model.
A driver-based example
Illustrative example: a service business plans 10 projects at an average fee of AED 20,000, producing AED 200,000 of revenue. At a 40% contribution margin and AED 60,000 of fixed costs, the simplified operating result is AED 20,000. If only eight projects complete, revenue falls to AED 160,000 and the result becomes AED 4,000, assuming the same margin and fixed costs. The useful discussion is which costs can change and when, not just the percentage reduction in revenue. This example excludes tax, financing and other adjustments.
How the work moves
Start with recent actual results and committed costs. Agree the operating drivers with their owners, build the model and test its calculations. Compare a small number of meaningful scenarios, then establish how actual results and changed assumptions will enter the next forecast version.
FP&A, financial modelling and cash-flow scenarios
Financial planning and analysis (FP&A) connects the forecast to actual results, explains the drivers of change and identifies the decisions behind the next version. A financial model may link profit and loss, balance sheet and cash flow where that is needed, rather than treating revenue growth as a substitute for a cash forecast. We define the model horizon, inputs, checks and update owner before work begins.
For a growth plan or funding-preparation project, the model can make headcount, customer growth, pricing, delivery costs, working capital and investment needs explicit. Unit economics or profitability scenarios can test contribution per customer, product or project when the data supports a consistent definition. Outputs can include a base case, downside sensitivities, cash runway and a documented assumptions register for management or investor-readiness discussions. Management owns the assumptions and decisions; models do not guarantee funding, valuation or future results.
Can you help if we have never prepared a budget?
Yes. Begin with the information available: current revenue, recurring expenses, payroll, planned purchases and known commitments. The model can develop as the quality of business data improves. Missing history should be identified, not replaced with unexplained precision.
How many scenarios do we need?
Enough to test the decision. A base case and one well-chosen downside case may be more useful than many variations. Each scenario should change a real driver and identify the management response it would trigger.
Will the forecast tell us whether we can afford an expansion?
It can help quantify the expected costs, timing and sensitivities. The answer also needs a cash view, funding assumptions and the consequences if revenue arrives later than planned. Forecasts inform the decision; they do not guarantee the outcome.
Who supplies the assumptions?
The people closest to sales, staffing, operations and spending supply the business inputs. LedgerByte helps structure and challenge the financial effect. Management remains responsible for the plan and the decisions based on it.

The service suits employers who need a repeatable preparation cycle and a reliable handover between HR, finance and the person authorizing payment.
What the work covers
Collect approved joiner, leaver, salary, attendance and variable-pay information.
Prepare salary calculations and payslips within the agreed scope.
Compare the current pay run with the previous period and explain material changes.
Prepare a WPS-ready file where applicable, using the employer's approved provider format.
Prepare payroll accounting journals and reconciliation schedules.

A payroll register, a change-and-variance summary, an exceptions list and the agreed payslips or payment-file preparation. The pack should reconcile employee-level amounts to the payroll total and distinguish salary cost, deductions and the net amount payable.
How the work moves
Set the cutoff. Identify who supplies and confirms each category of payroll change.
Calculate and compare. Prepare the pay run and check unexplained changes against the supporting instructions.
Resolve exceptions. Review incomplete employee details, unexpected deductions and changes received after cutoff.

Where WPS fits
The UAE Wages Protection System supports wage payments and regulatory monitoring. Establishments registered with MoHRE are required to pay wages through WPS or another system approved by the Ministry. Applicability, the responsible authority, provider requirements and the current payment timetable need to be checked for the specific employer, including free-zone arrangements.
Source check: 9 November 2026. A payroll review example
Illustrative example: last month's gross payroll was AED 120,000. This month's approved register totals AED 128,000. A useful variance bridge identifies AED 6,000 for a new employee and AED 2,000 in approved variable pay, explaining the AED 8,000 increase before deductions. The review still needs to check the supporting employee records and the separate net-payment totals.
Is preparing a WPS file the same as paying salaries?
No. Preparing the file is one step. The employer still needs the correct provider arrangement, validated employee details, sufficient funds and payment authorization. A file marked ready for review is not proof that salaries have been paid.
Can HR continue to manage employee information?
Yes. HR can remain the owner of employee records and approved changes while LedgerByte supports the calculation and accounting work. The cutoff and handover should make it clear which version of the employee data is being used.
What if a salary change arrives after cutoff?
It should be listed as an exception with the relevant period and supporting instruction. The employer decides how it should be handled in line with applicable requirements. Quietly replacing an already reviewed file makes the pay run harder to control.
Does this include employment-law or benefit advice?
No. Legal interpretations, employee entitlement decisions and disputes need the appropriate HR or legal advice. Payroll preparation uses the confirmed inputs and treatment supplied for the engagement.

Discuss your tax requirements
Separate tax workstreams. Connected accounting evidence.
Choose the workstream you need
VAT preparation and review support. Focus on the relevant return period, sales and purchase transactions, tax codes, imports, credit notes and reconciliations to the ledger. Identify items needing treatment review before the return figures are finalized.
Corporate tax filing. Prepare the computation, accounting-to-tax bridge and return inputs for the entity's tax period, with financial statements and supporting schedules. Reconcile relevant accounting balances and tax schedules.
Organize source documents and identify missing evidence.
Prepare the agreed registration application inputs, return workings or tax computation.
Track technical questions, client approval and the agreed authorized submission or filing handover.
What you receive
The output follows the service chosen: a VAT or corporate tax registration file, a VAT return pack, or a corporate tax computation and return pack. Practical UAE tax context
The FTA states that VAT returns and related payments are due within 28 days after the tax period ends. Use the period and due date assigned to the taxpayer, and check applicable FTA directions. Source check: 9 November 2026. [FTA: Filing VAT Returns and Making Payments](https://tax.gov.ae/en/content/filing.vat.returns.and.making.payments.aspx).
Under the general corporate tax rates, the first AED 375,000 of taxable income is taxed at 0%, with 9% on the amount above that threshold. Qualifying Free Zone Persons and other special regimes need their own assessment. The threshold relates to taxable income, not turnover. Source check: 9 November 2026. [FTA: Determination of Taxable Income, section 3.3](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Pdf/2024/Determination%20of%20Taxable%20Income%20-%2031%2007%202024.pdf).
Corporate tax returns and payment are generally due within nine months after the relevant tax period ends. Check the entity's actual obligations and any applicable FTA direction. Source check: 9 November 2026. [FTA filing reminder, 2 September 2026](https://tax.gov.ae/en/media.centre/news/federal.tax.authority.calls.on.all.persons.subject.to.corporate.tax.to.file.their.tax.returns.and.pay.the.corporate.tax.due.within.the.specified.timeframes.to.avoid.latepayment.penalties.aspx).
Why the accounting-to-tax bridge matters
Illustrative example, not a tax calculation: the ledger records an expense of AED 10,000. Whether all, part or none is deductible for corporate tax depends on the nature of the expense and the applicable rules. A preparation schedule preserves the original accounting amount, records the proposed tax adjustment and identifies its basis. Changing the bookkeeping entry simply to match a tax result can obscure what actually happened.
Can we start if our books are incomplete?
Yes, with a records assessment. Missing transactions and unreconciled balances may require bookkeeping cleanup before tax schedules can be supported. The initial scope should identify that dependency and the periods affected.
Are corporate tax and VAT thresholds interchangeable?
No. VAT registration considers taxable supplies and imports under its rules. The standard corporate tax rate threshold concerns taxable income. A business should not use its VAT registration status to conclude that it has no corporate tax obligations.
Does being in a free zone settle our tax treatment?
No. The entity's location is part of the assessment, not a complete answer. Qualifying Free Zone Person status and qualifying income require specific conditions to be considered. Bring the licence, activity description and transaction details into the initial discussion.
Can you guarantee there will be no penalties?
No. Compliance depends on the facts, complete records, correct treatment and required actions being completed on time. The preparation process is designed to make gaps and responsibilities visible; it cannot guarantee a tax outcome.

Illustrative example: opening cash is AED 50,000. Expected customer receipts are AED 80,000 and scheduled payments are AED 100,000, leaving AED 30,000 at the end of the forecast period. It does not mean the bank will permit an overdraft.
A weekly view can reveal an earlier shortfall even when the ending balance looks comfortable. Forecast receipts at the dates they are expected to arrive, rather than spreading a monthly total evenly without evidence.
How the work moves
Start with cleared cash and outstanding balances. Assign realistic dates to material receipts and payments, then challenge the assumptions with the people who own them. Review the forecast against actual bank movements, investigate the largest differences and record the next actions for collections, spending or funding discussions.
How is this different from a profit-and-loss report?
A profit-and-loss report measures income and expenses under the accounting basis. A cash forecast tracks when money enters and leaves the bank. Customer credit, inventory purchases, loan repayments and capital spending can create important differences between the two.
Is a 13-week forecast always the right answer?
No. Thirteen weeks is one useful format for short-term planning, but the horizon should reflect the decision and business cycle. Weekly detail may matter when cash is tight, while an annual plan needs a longer view. The level of detail is agreed around the purpose.
Will you chase customers or choose which suppliers get paid?
The service can identify overdue balances and proposed priorities. Customer collection activity, payment decisions and fund release remain with your team unless separately agreed. Supplier terms and operational consequences should be considered before changing payment timing.
How do you handle uncertain receipts?
Record the reason for uncertainty and test a later receipt date or a separate scenario. A disputed invoice should not automatically be treated as a normal on-time collection. Keeping those assumptions visible helps management see how much the cash view depends on them.

Month-End Close Checklist for Small Businesses | LedgerByte
A practical month-end close checklist covering records, reconciliations, adjustments and review, with a worked prepayment example and open-items template.
/insights/month-end-close
A practical month-end close checklist for a small business.
A month-end close brings the period's transactions and balances into a reviewable set of accounts. The aim is to know what is complete, what changed and which unresolved items could affect a decision.
Discuss your monthly close

Start with five questions
Before adding more spreadsheets, establish the basics:
A close checklist should make the work visible. Give each task an owner, a status, a link to its evidence and a reviewer where needed. “Done” should mean the task has an identifiable result, not that somebody opened the file.
Which entity and reporting period are being closed?
What accounting basis and policies apply?
Who supplies each source record, and what is the cutoff?
Which balances need reconciliation or supporting schedules?
Who reviews the close, and which issues must be escalated?
1. Gather the records and check completeness
Collect sales invoices, supplier bills, credit notes, expense claims, bank and card statements, payroll summaries and the schedules relevant to the business. Compare the available records with the period being closed. A month of transactions from one bank account does not show whether another account, card or payment processor is missing.
Look for gaps in invoice sequences where applicable, late supplier bills, duplicate uploads and transactions recorded under the wrong entity. Keep a missing-documents list with the person who can resolve each item. Avoid repeatedly asking the whole team for an unspecified “missing invoice.”
2. Reconcile bank, card and clearing balances
Compare each ledger balance with the corresponding statement or provider record. Match receipts and payments, then explain the remaining difference. Transfers between accounts, timing differences, fees and net settlements need particular attention.
Do not clear an unexplained difference simply by posting it to miscellaneous expenses. First establish whether it is a missing transaction, duplicate, wrong period or an item genuinely requiring a different accounting treatment. The reconciliation should show the statement balance, ledger balance and the items connecting them.
3. Review what customers owe and what the business owes
Check customer balances for receipts that have not been allocated, disputed invoices, overdue amounts and credits. Compare supplier balances with statements where available and investigate missing bills or payments posted to the wrong supplier.
Ageing reports are useful, but their quality depends on the source dates and allocations. An old outstanding amount may be a genuine collection issue or an unmatched payment. Those require different actions.
4. Prepare the period-end adjustments
Review the schedules relevant to the agreed accounting basis: accruals, prepayments, depreciation, inventory, loans, payroll balances and intercompany accounts. Document the evidence and calculation behind each proposed journal. Estimates should be labeled and reviewed rather than presented as confirmed invoices.
The month in which cash moves is not always the month in which the income or expense belongs. This is one reason a bank feed alone cannot complete an accrual-basis close.
Worked example: annual insurance paid upfront
Illustrative example under an accrual basis, excluding tax and other charges: a business pays AED 12,000 on 1 January for insurance covering January through December evenly. At the end of January, the monthly expense is AED 1,000 and the remaining prepayment is AED 11,000.
If the full AED 12,000 was initially posted to insurance expense, a proposed January adjustment moves AED 11,000 from expense to the prepayment asset. In February, AED 1,000 is released from that asset to insurance expense, leaving AED 10,000 prepaid. The original cash payment remains AED 12,000 in January; the adjustment changes the expense timing, not the bank movement.
Keep the policy document, coverage dates, payment evidence and monthly schedule together. Actual treatment depends on the policy, accounting basis and materiality; this is a teaching example, not advice on a particular entity's accounts.
5. Review the accounts for unusual movements
Read the profit and loss and balance sheet after the reconciliations and proposed adjustments. Compare them with a relevant prior period or budget. Investigate material changes in revenue, margin, payroll, receivables and balances that should normally clear.
The review should ask whether the movement makes sense given what happened in the business. It is not enough that the spreadsheet totals add up. A large repair cost might be real, misclassified or recorded twice; the supporting evidence decides which.
6. Close with an honest status report
A useful close pack includes the agreed accounts, completed reconciliations, supporting schedules, adjustments and an open-items list. Where your system and process allow, establish who can reopen a closed period and how changes will be recorded.
Use a simple open-item format:
This is more useful than a general statement that “the accounts are almost ready.”
Item: a supplier charge has no supporting invoice.
Period and amount: the affected month and known amount, if available.
Possible effect: the account or report that may change.
Owner and next action: who will obtain or assess the evidence.
Status: outstanding, resolved or included as a clearly identified estimate.
Before you circulate the pack
Every bank and card account has a reconciliation or a stated exception.
Major customer and supplier differences have an explanation.
Material journals have evidence, calculations and review status.
Missing information and estimates are visible.
The reporting period and version are clear.
The next action and owner are recorded for each material unresolved item.
How long should a close take?
There is no single timetable for every business. The volume and complexity of transactions, available records, systems and review requirements all matter. Set a realistic calendar after identifying the dependencies, then improve recurring delays instead of promising a fixed number of days without evidence.
Should we wait until every small question is resolved?
Not necessarily. The reviewer should consider materiality and the effect on the decisions being made. A pack can identify estimates and outstanding items, but it should not present an incomplete balance as final without explanation.
Can the close be automated?
Some imports, matching routines and recurring schedules can be automated. Missing evidence, unusual transactions and accounting judgments still need attention. Automation is useful when it makes exceptions clearer and leaves a traceable record of the work.
What should we fix first if every close is late?
Find the repeat bottleneck: late invoices, unreconciled opening balances, unclear ownership or a report rebuilt manually each month. Solve that dependency before expanding the checklist. The best first improvement is often a more reliable input cutoff and a named owner for missing information.

Worked example: positive profit, falling cash
Illustrative example for one month, using accrual accounting. All figures are in AED and exclude VAT, sales taxes, income tax, interest, inventory, owner transactions and other adjustments for simplicity. Assume there are no collections, payments or other movements relating to opening receivables and payables.
The profit-and-loss view is:
Now look at the cash movements:
Cash received is 60,000. Cash paid is 50,000 + 20,000 + 10,000 = 80,000. The bank balance therefore falls by 20,000, despite the 30,000 profit. If opening cash was 50,000, closing cash is 30,000.
Revenue: 100,000.
Operating expenses other than depreciation: 65,000.
Depreciation: 5,000.
Accounting profit: 30,000.
Customers paid 60,000 of the month's sales; 40,000 remains receivable.
The business paid 50,000 of the month's operating expenses; 15,000 remains payable.
It bought equipment for 20,000 in cash.
It repaid 10,000 of loan principal.
Build the bridge from profit to cash
The same example can be explained as a bridge:
This separates operating cash from investment and financing movements. It also prevents two common errors: counting depreciation as a current cash payment, and treating the full loan repayment as an operating expense. Actual financial statements may have additional adjustments and classification requirements.
Start with accounting profit of 30,000.
Add back non-cash depreciation of 5,000.
Subtract the 40,000 increase in receivables.
Add the 15,000 increase in payables.
Result: 10,000 of operating cash generated in this simplified example.
Subtract equipment spending of 20,000 and loan-principal repayment of 10,000.
Result: a 20,000 decrease in cash overall.
Ask which difference needs action
Not every movement needs the same response. Customer invoices that are not yet due need a realistic collection assumption. Disputed or overdue invoices may need follow-up. An increase in payables might reflect agreed credit terms, or it may indicate an overdue obligation that cannot simply be pushed further into the future.
Equipment spending may be a planned investment. Loan repayments may be contractually fixed. The purpose of the bridge is to identify the reason for the cash movement before choosing a response.
Turn the explanation into a dated forecast
A historical bridge explains what happened. A forecast estimates what will happen next. Start with the cleared bank balance, then list expected receipts and payments by date.
For a short-term view, include:
Use the lowest projected balance during the period as well as the ending balance. A customer receipt at month-end cannot fund a payroll payment due earlier unless the business has another source of cash.
Customer receipts with an expected collection date and the reason for that assumption.
Supplier payments using agreed terms and known commitments.
Payroll and other recurring operating payments.
Tax payments, loan payments and planned capital spending.
Any committed funding, separately identified from financing still being discussed.
Test one realistic delay
Illustrative example: a forecast starts with 30,000 of cash, expects 70,000 of receipts and includes 80,000 of payments. It ends with 20,000. If a 25,000 customer receipt moves beyond the forecast horizon, the ending balance becomes negative 5,000.
The scenario does not predict that the customer will be late. It shows that the plan depends on that receipt arriving. The practical next step is to verify the expected payment date, examine flexible spending and consider the available options before the gap arrives.
A weekly cash-review checklist
A forecast becomes more useful when its past estimates are compared with reality. Continually moving an overdue receipt into the next week without explanation can make the model look healthier than the underlying position.
Replace the completed week with actual bank movements.
Explain the largest receipt and payment timing differences.
Reconfirm major customer collection dates.
Add new commitments and remove items already paid.
Keep disputed or uncertain receipts clearly marked.
Review the lowest projected cash point and the actions needed.
Record who owns each follow-up and when the assumption will be checked again.
Does negative cash flow mean the business is unprofitable?
Not necessarily. Cash can fall because of growing receivables, inventory, equipment investment or debt repayment. The cause matters. Equally, positive cash flow can come from borrowing or delaying payments even when operating performance is weak.
Should we use a profit forecast or a cash forecast?
Use both when the decision needs both. The profit forecast tests revenue and costs; the cash forecast tests timing and funding. A growth plan may look profitable while requiring cash before the related sales are collected.
Is the bank balance enough for a cash review?
It is the starting point. It does not show which receipts are expected, what is committed or what falls due next. Reconciled balances and a dated commitments schedule provide the context.
What is working capital?
In this practical context, working-capital review focuses on money tied up in items such as customer receivables and inventory, alongside supplier payment terms and balances. Different analyses use different definitions, so specify the measure before comparing periods or businesses.

Build a review-ready UAE VAT records pack.
A useful VAT pack lets the reviewer trace the return back to transactions and supporting evidence. This guide covers the preparation checklist, a simplified calculation and the questions to resolve before the return is finalized.
Discuss your VAT records

1. Confirm the taxpayer and return period
Start with the correct legal entity, TRN and return period. Keep the prior return and the opening VAT control-account position available. Where several entities share staff or systems, confirm that the records have not been mixed.
The FTA states that VAT returns and related payments are due within 28 days after the end of the tax period. Check the taxpayer's actual due date and allow time for review and payment. Source check: 9 November 2026. [FTA: Filing VAT Returns and Making Payments](https://tax.gov.ae/en/content/filing.vat.returns.and.making.payments.aspx).
2. Assemble the transaction schedules
Prepare listings that preserve a reference back to each source document:
Keep zero-rated, exempt and out-of-scope categories distinct for review. They are different treatments, even if no VAT amount appears on an individual transaction. Do not decide the category from the customer's location or a software default alone.
Sales invoices and sales credit notes, with dates, values, tax codes and customer details needed for review.
Purchase invoices and purchase credit notes, including supporting tax documentation.
Import and customs records, with amounts reconciled to the accounting records.
Overseas-service purchases and other transactions needing reverse-charge consideration.
Adjustments and unusual transactions with a clear explanation.
3. Check evidence and treatment before totaling the return
Confirm that the transaction belongs to the entity and period under review, that supporting documents are available and that the tax code reflects the treatment being applied. Flag transactions requiring technical judgment rather than guessing a category to finish the spreadsheet.
Input VAT is not automatically recoverable because an expense appears in the accounts. The documentation, purpose of the cost, applicable restrictions and recovery timing need to be considered. Source check: 9 November 2026. [FTA: VAT Returns User Guide, input-tax section](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Pdf/VAT%20Returns%20User%20GuideEnglishV40%2015%2008%202021%20SEP2021.pdf).
Worked example: a simple net VAT calculation
Hypothetical illustration only. Assume a UAE VAT-registered business has only standard-rated transactions for this example, all items fall in the correct return period, the credit note is valid, all purchase VAT shown is fully recoverable and no other adjustments apply. The UAE's standard VAT rate is 5%. Source check: 9 November 2026. [FTA: Standard VAT rate](https://tax.gov.ae/en/faq.aspx?keyword=What+is+the+standard+rate+of+VAT+in+the+UAE%3F).
This is an explanation of the arithmetic, not a completed return or a conclusion that a particular business can recover all purchase VAT. Imports, reverse charge, mixed-use costs, exempt activities, adjustments and other facts may change the actual result.
Sales excluding VAT: AED 100,000. Output VAT: AED 5,000.
Sales credit note excluding VAT: AED 10,000. Output VAT reduction: AED 500.
Net output VAT: AED 4,500.
Eligible purchases excluding VAT: AED 40,000. Recoverable input VAT: AED 2,000.
Simplified net VAT payable: AED 4,500 minus AED 2,000 = AED 2,500.
4. Reconcile the schedules to the books
Compare the sales schedule with the relevant revenue and receivable records, and the purchase schedule with the expense, asset and payable records. Investigate differences caused by missing credit notes, duplicated invoices, wrong-period entries or tax coding.
Then reconcile the VAT control account. Explain the relationship between its opening balance, period postings, payments or refunds, adjustments and closing balance. The ending ledger balance is not automatically identical to the current return's payment amount because it can contain earlier-period items.
In the worked example, the supporting schedule explains the AED 500 reduction for the sales credit note. If the ledger still shows AED 5,000 of output VAT, that difference needs investigation. A balancing entry without the credit note reference would hide the reason for the change.
5. Keep a separate exceptions list
A review-ready pack can contain unresolved questions, provided they are visible. For each one, record the transaction, amount, tax period, issue, evidence needed and responsible person.
Examples include a missing tax invoice, an import value that differs from the ledger, a credit note relating to an earlier transaction or a purchase used for both business and non-business purposes. The reviewer can then assess the treatment and timing based on the facts. Do not assume every missing document can simply be claimed later without considering the relevant rules.
6. Complete the review and filing handover
Identify who prepares the schedules, resolves technical questions, approves the figures and is authorized to submit. Retain the final workings and the actual submission acknowledgement and payment evidence when available. A spreadsheet marked “final” is not evidence that a return was filed or paid.
Use a secure, agreed document process. Do not put EmaraTax passwords, bank credentials or full employee records into a general contact form or email thread.
A final readiness checklist
Entity, TRN, period and due date are confirmed.
Sales and purchase listings include relevant credit notes.
Import and other specialist-treatment records are included where applicable.
Tax codes and input-tax recovery questions have been reviewed.
Differences between schedules and the ledger are explained.
Open issues have an owner and a clear next action.
The approval and authorized submission route is known.
Final workings, filing acknowledgement and payment evidence have a defined place in the records.
Are bank statements a substitute for tax invoices?
No. Bank statements show money movements. The VAT review needs the relevant tax documentation and transaction facts. They are useful supporting records, but do not by themselves establish the right to input-tax recovery.
What if the ledger total differs from the return schedule?
Investigate the difference by transaction and period. Common causes include credit notes, posting dates, payments relating to an earlier return or incorrect tax coding. Keep an explanation that another reviewer can follow rather than forcing the two totals to match.
Should we include an earlier-period error in the next return?
First assess the required correction route. The correct treatment depends on the facts and applicable rules. Record the error and its evidence separately so it is not silently absorbed into current-period transactions.
Does this checklist establish that our tax treatment is correct?
No. It helps organize the evidence and review process. Registration, place of supply, recovery restrictions, corrections and other technical matters still depend on the specific transactions and current rules.

Build a supported Saudi VAT process, from registration readiness and invoice records to reconciled return workings and approval packs.
/finance/services/ksa-vat
Make Saudi VAT traceable from the invoice to the return.
LedgerByte supports Saudi VAT-registration readiness, transaction reviews and return preparation. The focus is a repeatable process that connects the reported figures to the records behind them and brings unresolved treatments into view before sign-off.
Discuss your Saudi VAT requirements
Registration readiness. Supported records. Reconciled VAT returns.
When this service fits
You are starting Saudi operations, approaching a registration threshold, preparing your first return or inheriting a VAT ledger that does not match previous filings. The scope can cover a one-off assessment, cleanup for specified periods or recurring VAT preparation alongside your accounting team.
Establish the registration position
For a Saudi-resident business, mandatory VAT registration tests whether taxable supplies exceeded SAR 375,000 in the previous twelve months or are expected to exceed that amount in the next twelve months. Voluntary registration may be available above SAR 187,500 of taxable supplies or taxable expenses, subject to the rules. Non-resident persons required to account for Saudi VAT need a separate assessment; the resident threshold is not a safe assumption for them. [ZATCA registration guidance, section 7](https://www.zatca.gov.sa/en/HelpCenter/guidelines/Documents/VAT-Guideline-for-Electronic-Contracts.pdf). Source check: 9 November 2026.
We prepare the supporting turnover analysis, review expected activity and identify the dates and evidence requiring confirmation. Total bank receipts are not used as a substitute for a taxable-supplies assessment.
Build the return from supported records
Invoice mismatches remain visible exceptions to resolve before sign-off.
Map sales and purchases to the relevant VAT categories and flag uncertain treatments.
Reconcile sales records, credit notes and VAT control accounts to the ledger.
Review purchase evidence and identify amounts needing an input-tax eligibility decision.
Assemble import records and cross-border transaction information where relevant.
Track adjustments, missing documents and differences from prior returns.
Prepare the return workings and a review pack showing the source of each reported amount.
What to have ready
The registration certificate if issued, previous returns, the VAT ledger, sales and purchase listings, invoice samples, credit notes, contracts for unusual transactions and relevant import documents. Confirm the entity, period and accounting-system cut-off so the same transaction is not included twice.
You receive registration-readiness findings where requested, reconciled return workings, an exceptions log and a sign-off pack. Submission is completed only through the appropriately authorized taxpayer or representative, with local qualified advice where required.
Set a workable reporting sequence
Agree the data cut-off, complete reconciliations, resolve material questions and obtain approval before filing. ZATCA's guidance requires the VAT return and payment of net VAT due by the last day of the month following the tax period. Confirm the entity's monthly or quarterly period before setting its calendar. [ZATCA VAT filing guidance, section 9.3](https://zatca.gov.sa/en/HelpCenter/guidelines/Documents/Guideline-on-Tax-Groups-under-VAT-Provisions.pdf). Source check: 9 November 2026.
Can we assess registration before the first sale?
Yes. We can organize the expected sales, startup expenditure and supporting contracts for review. Eligibility, the applicable calculation period and the effective registration date need confirmation against the business's circumstances. An estimate alone does not establish registration status.
Can you prepare returns while our team keeps the books?
Yes. Agree the ledger cut-off, document responsibilities and treatment-review process. Our preparation pack can build on your team's records, with any cleanup identified separately so it does not become an unexplained recurring adjustment.
Does e-invoicing integration replace a VAT return?
No. ZATCA describes e-invoicing integration and VAT-return submission as separate processes. We can review accounting-side readiness and coordinate questions with your software provider. Software implementation or certification is not included in this VAT scope. [E-invoicing phases](https://zatca.gov.sa/en/E-Invoicing/Introduction/Pages/Roll-out-phases.aspx) and [VAT-return journey](https://zatca.gov.sa/en/HelpCenter/CustomerJourney/Pages/tax-journey.aspx).
What if a previous return does not match the accounts?
We trace the difference by period and document the proposed treatment for review. Amendments, disclosures and authority correspondence require a separately agreed scope and authorization. We do not simply carry an unexplained difference into the next return.

ZATCA Filing & Tax Preparation Support | LedgerByte
Coordinate Saudi VAT, Zakat, income tax and withholding tax preparation with defined obligations, supported schedules and authorized sign-off.
/finance/services/zatca-filing
Give every Saudi tax filing its own evidence, owner and review.
LedgerByte helps organize ZATCA return preparation across the obligations relevant to your business. Start with the entity's tax position, then build the schedules, review decisions and filing calendar around it.
Review your ZATCA filing requirements
Separate obligations. Coordinated records. Clear approval steps.
Establish which obligations apply
“ZATCA filing” can refer to several different returns. A VAT registration does not establish the treatment of the business for every other tax. We start with legal form, ownership, residency, activities, financial year, existing registrations and cross-border payments.
Ownership and structure matter: ZATCA's income-tax guidance addresses non-Saudi interests in resident capital companies and non-resident business or income within the Kingdom. The assessment must use the actual facts rather than a single rule for every Saudi entity. [ZATCA income-tax framework](https://www.zatca.gov.sa/en/RulesRegulations/Taxes/Pages/IncomeTaxlaw.aspx). Source check: 9 November 2026.
Keep the preparation streams distinct
The engagement records which streams are included and which require specialist review. Customs declarations, excise tax, objections and other filings are not assumed to be part of this scope.
VAT: track the relevant period, approved VAT workings and the separate filing and payment steps. Detailed transaction preparation is covered by our KSA VAT service.
Zakat: organize the financial statements and balance-sheet schedules needed for the applicable Zakat-base review. Zakat preparation is not simply a percentage applied to sales. [ZATCA balance-sheet treatment resource](https://zatca.gov.sa/en/HelpCenter/ZakatItems/Pages/default.aspx).
Income tax: assemble the trial balance, supporting accounts, tax-adjustment schedules and ownership information for the applicable annual return.
Withholding tax: review the register of payments to non-residents, contracts, payment dates and treatment questions. Applicability depends on the payment and relevant rules; treaty treatment is assessed separately. [ZATCA withholding-tax guideline](https://zatca.gov.sa/en/HelpCenter/guidelines/Documents/General-Guideline-for-Withholding-Tax-In-accordance-with-the-provisions-of-the-Income-Tax-Law-and-its-Implementing-Regulations.pdf).
Build the calendar from the entity's facts
We confirm the periods and open obligations, then work backwards from filing dates to the records cut-off and approval meeting. ZATCA identifies a 120-day deadline after the relevant year-end for annual Zakat and corporate income-tax returns. This should not be applied to VAT or monthly withholding-tax returns. [ZATCA annual-return deadline guidance](https://zatca.gov.sa/en/MediaCenter/News/Pages/Submit-CIT-Return-for-2025.aspx) and [monthly withholding-tax service](https://zatca.gov.sa/en/eServices/Pages/eservices-043.aspx). Source check: 9 November 2026.
What you provide and receive
Provide the ownership structure, registration details, prior filings, financial statements, current trial balance, relevant balance schedules, non-resident payment records and outstanding authority notices. Access and sensitive records are handled through an agreed secure process.
You receive an obligations checklist, preparation calendar, supporting schedules and an issues register. The sign-off pack identifies the return version, unresolved decisions, approver and submission responsibility. Filing receipts and payment evidence are retained when supplied by the authorized filer and payer.
Does every Saudi company need all four returns?
No. We determine the relevant obligations from ownership, legal form, activities, residency, transactions and registrations. Some businesses need several preparation streams. Others do not. A group structure or ownership change should be reviewed before reusing last year's assumptions.
Who approves and submits the return?
Management approves the facts and final treatment. Submission is carried out by the appropriately authorized taxpayer or representative, with a locally qualified adviser involved where required. Preparation support does not itself confer authority to file or replace regulated professional work.
Should overseas supplier payments wait until the annual tax review?
No. Put relevant payments into a review register as they occur, with contracts, beneficiary details and payment dates. This allows withholding questions and the applicable monthly workflow to be assessed without relying on an annual reconstruction.
Can you help with overdue returns or a ZATCA query?
We can first organize the affected periods, notices and available evidence. Catch-up preparation, correction work and responses to the authority are then scoped separately, with the required authorization and specialist input. No penalty relief or authority outcome is promised.

Support before establishment

Saudi establishment requirements need their own review. MISA's framework distinguishes investment registration from subsequent commercial registration and relevant activity permissions. The correct route cannot be assumed solely from an existing UAE registration. [MISA investment framework](https://misa.gov.sa/activities/laws-regulations-copy/). Source check: 9 November 2026.
Support for an operating business
Start with the missing foundation. An unsupported opening balance can affect both management reporting and return preparation. A cleanup phase may therefore be needed before a recurring monthly timetable is reliable.
Accounting and bookkeeping: post supported transactions, reconcile balances and maintain a month-end issues list.

Can we start with one overdue period rather than outsourcing everything?
Yes. A defined reconciliation or return-preparation project can establish the baseline. We identify opening-balance issues and missing evidence, then agree whether recurring bookkeeping, reporting or controller support would help maintain the result.
Can you coordinate with our existing Saudi adviser?
Yes, subject to an agreed scope and information-sharing authorization. We can prepare schedules and maintain a questions list for their review. Any regulated advice, assurance or representation is confirmed under the appropriate engagement.
Where does e-invoicing fit?
It belongs in the accounting-process review, including invoice data, responsibility for exceptions and readiness for applicable ZATCA requirements. Phase Two is rolled out by taxpayer group, so the business's applicable notice and requirements need checking. [ZATCA e-invoicing phases](https://zatca.gov.sa/en/E-Invoicing/Introduction/Pages/Roll-out-phases.aspx). Accounting-side coordination is scoped here; wider technology work belongs at LedgerByte Tech.

Close the period with the balances explained.
Give each reporting period a defined finish. LedgerByte supports month-end and year-end close work, bringing reconciliations, adjustment schedules and outstanding questions into a reviewable pack.
Discuss your close process
Reconciled balances. Documented adjustments. A clear handover.
When this service fits
Your team posts transactions throughout the month, but the final checks keep slipping. Balance-sheet schedules do not agree to the ledger, late invoices change the reported result, or year-end questions require rebuilding records that should already be available. Close support gives this work its own checklist, responsibilities and review points.
The engagement can support an existing bookkeeper or finance team. It focuses on completing and substantiating a reporting period; ongoing transaction processing, management oversight and a fully outsourced finance function are separate scopes.
Month-end and year-end have different needs
A month-end close establishes a consistent reporting cut-off. The work can include bank and control-account reconciliations, accruals, prepayments, depreciation schedules and explanations for unusual movements. Open issues remain visible so reviewers can judge whether the period is ready for reporting.
Year-end builds on those monthly records. It may require a fuller review of balance-sheet schedules, supporting documents for estimates, proposed year-end adjustments and a coordinated handover to tax or audit advisers. The applicable reporting basis and adviser requirements are agreed at the outset. Tax calculations, statutory financial statement preparation and external audit work are separately scoped.
How the close moves
The close calendar reflects when records arrive and who approves outstanding items.
Set the baseline. Confirm the entity, period, reporting basis, last completed close and outstanding prior-period issues.
Complete the reconciliations. Compare ledger balances with statements and supporting records, and investigate differences.
Prepare adjustments. Document proposed entries, calculations and evidence, with accounting judgments referred to the designated reviewer.
Review and finalize. Obtain approval for agreed entries, refresh the schedules and record unresolved matters and their owners.
Hand over the pack. Provide the agreed reporting extracts and adviser schedules, identifying changes made after review.
What you receive and what to prepare
The agreed deliverables can include a close checklist, reconciled trial balance, balance-sheet schedules, adjustment log and open-items register. A year-end pack can also include fixed-asset movements, loan reconciliations and schedules requested by the business's advisers. Each schedule should tie to the final ledger version.
Have the accounting records, prior close pack, bank statements, loan documents, asset register, payroll summaries and relevant customer or supplier records ready. Tell us about transactions near period-end and estimates requiring management input. Access to records is arranged after the scope is agreed.
Can you handle the close while our team keeps the books?
Yes. We agree where daily processing ends and close work begins. Your team can retain invoicing and transaction entry while LedgerByte prepares reconciliations and adjustment schedules. Clear ownership helps avoid duplicate entries and competing versions of the trial balance.
What happens when an invoice arrives after month-end?
We check the underlying transaction, relevant period and supporting evidence. For example, a supplier invoice received later may relate to services already delivered. Any proposed accrual or other adjustment is documented for review under the agreed accounting policies, rather than assigned solely by receipt date.
Can you work with our tax accountant or external auditor?
Yes, where authorized. We can prepare agreed schedules, organize evidence and track information requests. Management retains responsibility for approvals, and each adviser retains responsibility for their own work. LedgerByte close support does not provide a statutory audit opinion or assurance conclusion.
What if earlier periods are still unreconciled?
We identify which opening balances need investigation and separate catch-up work from the current close. An unsupported balance should not disappear into a new period without explanation. The plan sets out what can be completed and what remains dependent on missing records.

Discuss your receivables process
Accurate billing. Matched receipts. Visible next steps.
When this service fits
Customer payments arrive without remittance details. An overdue report mixes late payments with unresolved credits and disputed invoices. Receivables support brings these records together before the next follow-up.
Broader bookkeeping, cash-flow forecasting and finance leadership are separately scoped.
What the work covers
Sending invoices or contacting customers is agreed explicitly. The arrangement identifies which customers may be contacted, the information that may be shared, the communication channel and when an issue must return to your team. Ledger access alone does not authorize customer communication.
Prepare or issue invoices from approved billing instructions and supporting records, within the agreed workflow.
Check customer references, payment terms and billing details against approved information.
Allocate receipts to invoices using bank records, remittance advice and customer account history.
Reconcile the customer ledger and investigate credits, unapplied cash and balance differences.
Maintain ageing reports and distinguish overdue invoices from disputed or unresolved items.
Track routine customer queries and authorized follow-up, with an owner and next action for each exception.
How the work moves
For example, a customer may pay several invoices together while withholding an amount they dispute. The supported portion can be allocated, the disputed item tracked separately, and the difference referred for review. Recording the whole account as settled would conceal the issue; chasing the whole original balance would ignore the payment.
Review the starting position. Compare the customer ledger, open invoices, receipts and credit notes, including older balances.
Establish the billing routine. Agree the evidence, approvals and responsibilities needed before an invoice is issued.
Match money to balances. Allocate supported receipts and place uncertain allocations on an exceptions list.
Review outstanding items. Separate timing differences, missing documents, disputes and amounts awaiting payment.
Follow up and report. Carry out agreed routine contact and return decisions outside the approved scope to the responsible person.
What you receive and what to prepare
Deliverables can include a reconciled receivables listing, ageing report, unallocated-receipts log, dispute register and follow-up tracker. Estimated collection dates and customer promises are identified separately from cash received.
Prepare the customer ledger, invoice and credit-note records, bank receipts, remittance advice, approved terms and relevant billing evidence. Your team also identifies who can authorize credits, refunds, write-offs and changes to commercial terms. Those decisions remain with your designated approvers.
Can you raise invoices using information from our sales team?
Yes, using an agreed approval process and sufficient billing evidence. We establish which records confirm the amount, customer and billing milestone. Incomplete or conflicting instructions are returned for clarification instead of becoming an unsupported invoice.
Will you chase overdue customers for us?
We can carry out specifically authorized routine reminders and statement follow-up. The agreed boundaries cover recipients, wording, frequency and escalation. Disputes, threatened legal action, settlement offers or changed payment terms go back to your team unless separately authorized and within scope.
How do you handle payments that cannot be identified?
We check available bank references, remittances and customer records before allocating the receipt. If the evidence is insufficient, it remains separately tracked for investigation. Guessing at an allocation can leave the wrong invoice overdue and make later reconciliations harder.
Does the service guarantee payment or include legal recovery?
No. It improves the records and routine supporting collection, but customers may still delay or dispute payment. Credit decisions, legal debt recovery and guarantees of collection are outside this service. We keep the evidence and status clear so your team can decide the next step.

An invoice that passes a data check still needs evidence that the purchase was authorized and goods or services received.
Log incoming invoices and check key details against the records available.
Compare invoices with purchase orders, delivery records or agreed evidence of services received where applicable.
Code bills to the agreed accounts and dimensions, referring uncertain treatment for review.
Flag possible duplicates, missing documents, unexpected charges and unmatched credit notes.

We flag the request and refer it to your designated verifier. Your team independently verifies and authorizes changes using its approved process. Changed instructions are not accepted solely because they appear on an invoice or in a supplier email.
Can you help with old or disputed supplier balances?
